question: Before 2002, which UN diplomats in New York ran up the most unpaid parking tickets per diplomat?
answer: Those from high-corruption countries. Diplomatic immunity meant no fine could be enforced, so only habit restrained them. Fisman and Miguel found unpaid tickets tracked corruption at home, even allowing for national income. When New York began removing diplomatic plates for unpaid fines in 2002, violations fell by about 98%. Norms mattered; enforcement mattered more.
move: When nobody can be punished, behaviour shows the habits people brought.
ask: How do I behave when nobody can hold me to account?
trap: Assuming rich countries' diplomats simply shrug off fines they can afford.
reference: Fisman & Miguel, Corruption, Norms, and Legal Enforcement: Evidence from Diplomatic Parking Tickets, Journal of Political Economy, 2007
